proposals.title: Model-level tests for cache restore and Strava/Health merge
proposals.body:
## Summary
The Stay-connected feature pulled the Health/Strava merge out into `WorkoutMerge.compose` (Sources/AppCore/WorkoutMerge.swift) and gave it unit tests (Tests/AppCoreTests/WorkoutMergeTests.swift, ActivityHistoryTests.swift). The model paths that call it in Sources/AppCore/Model.swift still have no tests: restoring the snapshot cache on a cold launch, a Health refresh that keeps Strava workouts, and `clearStravaWorkouts` / `clearCachedSnapshot`. The user accepted this gap at the Save gate, so it's follow-up work.

## Key Decisions
- Test through the model's public surface with an injected cache store, not through UI scenarios. Scenario seeds bypass the merge, so a capture can't show it.
- Use fixed dates so the newest-activity ordering is deterministic.

## Implementation
1. Add `Tests/AppCoreTests/ModelHistoryPersistenceTests.swift`.
2. Cold launch: write a cached snapshot, build a new model, and assert that history and the newest activity load before any network call.
3. Health refresh: seed Strava workouts, run a Health refresh, and assert the Strava entries are still there and the merged list is in order.
4. Clearing: assert that `clearStravaWorkouts` removes only Strava entries and that `clearCachedSnapshot` empties the persisted snapshot.
5. Register the tests with descriptions.
proposals.reason: The merge logic is tested, but the model paths that use it aren't: cold-launch restore, Health refresh keeping Strava runs, and clearing the caches.

proposals.title: Two planned demos have no screenshot: merged Health + Strava history with duplicates removed, and a Strava-only relaunch. Screenshot setups skip the merge by design.
proposals.body:
## Summary

Two planned demos have no screenshot: merged Health + Strava history with duplicates removed, and a Strava-only relaunch. Screenshot setups skip the merge by design.

At the approval gate for "Stay connected and keep full history across launches" the user approved the built work past this gap: it differs from what the plan asked for. Built from plan `stay-connected-and-keep-full-history-across-launches` (now at `.codeyam/plans/completed/stay-connected-and-keep-full-history-across-launches.md`).

Your Strava and Health history now survives relaunching the app, and refreshing one source no longer wipes out the other.

## What you can now do
- Reopen the app and still see your full workout history, Strava runs included
- Refresh Health data without losing runs that came from Strava
- Use Strava alone and still see your newest activity on Today
- Count on the merge logic: it has its own tests, 522/522 passing

Read that plan and the code it changed before planning how to close the gap.

proposals.title: register-test fix command omits required --file
proposals.body:
## What happened
REGISTRY_TEST_MISSING_DESCRIPTION's fixCommand prints `register-test` without `--file`, which is rejected. `backfill-descriptions` does not support the Swift `tests` runner, so 36 tests had to be removed and re-registered by hand, then `refresh-tests --force` run to restore evidence.

## What would have helped
A fixCommand that runs as printed, and backfill-descriptions support for the Swift runner (reading descriptions from the test's leading `//` comment).
proposals.reason: The suggested fix for missing test descriptions is rejected when run as printed.

proposals.title: start-simulator picks an iOS 18.1 device that mismatches committed captures
proposals.body:
## What happened
start-simulator silently defaulted to an iOS 18.1 device; its frames differ from the committed iOS 26 set (flat tab bar), so every recapture would show as changed. Had to manually boot the iOS 26.5 iPhone 17 Pro.

## What would have helped
Pick the device/runtime that matches the committed captures (record it alongside them), or warn loudly on mismatch.
proposals.reason: Recaptures came out with a different (flat) tab bar than the committed iOS 26 screenshots.

proposals.title: recapture-stale per-scenario time budget too short under load
proposals.body:
## What happened
recapture-stale derived a 16s/scenario budget, but captures took 40-120s under host load; slugs failed with a bare "error sending request" when the per-capture request timed out.

## What would have helped
A budget derived from observed capture times, and a timeout error that names the budget exceeded.
proposals.reason: Captures failed with a bare 'error sending request' when they exceeded a 16s budget.

proposals.title: Finalize coverage silently invalidated by a later .gitignore edit
proposals.body:
## What happened
`.codeyam/state/finalize-debt.json` was gitignored, which only surfaced at verify-full-finalize after a full finalize. Un-ignoring it changed .gitignore after the finalize, so `push` refused with 'not yet finalized' even though session-finalize had just reported status=ok; a second finalize was needed.

## What would have helped
Don't gitignore the coverage marker by default (or flag it at scaffold/first finalize), and have the commit step warn when files change after the finalize it relies on.
proposals.reason: Push was refused after a passing finalize because .gitignore changed afterwards; finalize had to be re-run.

proposals.title: The closed-app wiring — the iPhone background refresh task, the Health wake hook, and sending the heartbeat only after fresh data — has no automated test; it is iPhone-only code, and only the decisions it relies on are tested.
proposals.body:
## Summary

The closed-app wiring — the iPhone background refresh task, the Health wake hook, and sending the heartbeat only after fresh data — has no automated test; it is iPhone-only code, and only the decisions it relies on are tested.

At the approval gate for "Battery-light background refresh" the user approved the built work past this gap: it differs from what the plan asked for. Built from plan `battery-light-background-refresh` (now at `.codeyam/plans/completed/battery-light-background-refresh.md`).

Otterpace now keeps your activity data fresh on its own, without opening the app and without draining the battery.

## What you can now do
- Open the app and see up-to-date numbers (refreshes on foreground, at most every 15 min)
- Get coaching nudges based on fresh movement data, piggybacking on HealthKit wakes iOS already grants
- Have Strava re-sync in the background every few hours via one long-interval iOS refresh task
- Pull-to-refresh still forces an immediate update; the AI coach never runs while the app is closed

Read that plan and the code it changed before planning how to close the gap.
proposals.reason: Approved past at the approval gate for "Battery-light background refresh".
